programs.label: NSA Information Systems Security Professionals Certification (Cybersecurity)
programs.description: All undergraduate Computer Science students who take CS 457, CS 458 and CS 482 receive the NSA-approved "Information Systems Security Professionals Certification." Students learn cybersecurity tools and techniques to protect networks and systems from attackers, preparing them for the nation's shortage of technical cybersecurity expertise.
programs.note: With permission of the Cybersecurity Office, and only in special circumstances, CS 482 may be replaced by a relevant course; record an approved substitute as credit for CS 482 (source Waived) with a note. CS 457 is offered in fall only and CS 458 in spring only, so plan CS 457 in the fall before CS 458. The courses also count as CS electives.
claimSteps: Take the transcript to the CS Admin Assistant (King Hall 219B) or email it to hopperlg@jmu.edu.

groups.label: Required courses
groups.note: CS 457 Information Security, CS 458 Cyber Defense, CS 482 Selected Topics in Information Security.

programs.label: Robotics minor
programs.note: 20–21 credits (2026–27 catalog). Basic preparation (programming, calculus, physics) can be waived by the minor advisor for a comparable course or experience. At least one elective must come from a different department than the core course. CISE 481 summarizes a capstone robotics project: the student must have completed or be enrolled in an approved capstone, special topics or independent study course with a robotics project, or, at the advisor's discretion, an internship, research or professional project in robotics. Coordinator: Nathan Sprague (spragunr@jmu.edu).

groups.label: Basic preparation: physics
groups.note: PHYS 140/140L and PHYS 240/240L also meet General Education Physical Principles and Lab Experience. Students who completed Physical Principles with a course not listed should meet with the minor advisor.
